relation: sheet 8 lies WEST of sheet 29; shared street Av. G or Winnie E.
overlap_description: There is NO two-dimensional drawn overlap. Sheet 8's map content stops dead on the WEST property line of Av. G (fitted x = 3087-3102 depending on y); everything east of it on sheet 8 is blank paper carrying only the rotated legends 'AV. G OR WINNIE E.', 'SEE SHEET No 29.', the avenue width label 70', and Av.-G house numbers. Sheet 29's map content starts on the EAST property line of Av. G (fitted x = 257-290); everything west of it is blank paper carrying 'AV. G OR WINNIE E.', 'SEE SHEET No 8.', 70', and house numbers. The 70-ft roadway itself is drawn in full by NEITHER sheet: the west line of Av. G would fall at x~45-78 on sheet 29, i.e. under the torn/tilted paper edge, and the east line would fall at x~3300-3315 on sheet 8, which is blank. What the two sheets DO share is the eight EAST-WEST street property lines that cross the avenue: each of the four numbered streets in this row has its north and south property line drawn on both sheets, sheet 8 from x~1728-3100 and sheet 29 from x~257-1085. Those eight shared lines, plus the printed and independently measured 70-ft avenue width, are the entire basis of the correspondences below. Every correspondence therefore lies on one straight line (the avenue centreline) - this seam is intrinsically ONE-DIMENSIONAL. See notes.

Its spacing from the next line down is 246.2 px (sheet 8) and 247.8 px (sheet 29) = the printed 80-ft street width, so it cannot be confused with a block line. Both sheets draw it right up to the Av. rejected_candidates.feature: A one-block (two-street-line) vertical shift of the pairing
rejected_candidates.reason: Excluded on four independent grounds: (1) both sheets draw exactly eight E-W property lines in the alternating 246 / 923 / 245 / 919 / 246 / 923 / 247 px pattern (80 ft street, ~300 ft block) between their top and bottom coverage limits, with none to spare; (2) both bottom continuation notes point into row B (No 10 on sheet 8, No 27 on sheet 29), so the bottom lines are the same street; (3) the Av.-G frontage house numbers facing each other across the avenue in the top row are both in the 1500 block (1501-1504 on sheet 8, 1510-1511 on sheet 29); (4) the named blocks - Central Park and Ball High School on sheet 29, Winnie House/Fleming Livery and Casino Hall on sheet 8 - line up row for row.

rejected_candidates.feature: Blind template matching / NCC across the seam
rejected_candidates.reason: Not attempted, per the brief - and in any case impossible here, because there is no drawn overlap at all for a template to match.

notes:
METHOD. Every feature was identified semantically first (printed avenue name, printed street widths, block numbers, named buildings, house numbers, reciprocal continuation notes) and only then measured. Measurement was by intensity-weighted centroid of the ink of the heavy continuous property line, with the horizontal street line fitted robustly over 340 px (sheet 8, x 2745-3085) or 750 px (sheet 29, x 300-1050) and the vertical Av.-G frontage line fitted over each block's full 900 px height; the corner is the intersection of the two fitted centrelines, solved iteratively. Per-line fit rms was 0.08-0.66 px. Four corners were additionally verified by eye at 12-14x magnification with a 1-source-pixel grid overlay (crops in output/qc/manual_crops/).

THE 70-FT CONSTRUCTION - read this before using the points. Because neither sheet draws the far side of Av. G, no ground point is drawn on both sheets. Each correspondence is therefore the intersection of a shared E-W street property line with the CENTRELINE of Av. G, constructed as: a_x = (sheet-8 west frontage x) + W8/2, b_x = (sheet-29 east frontage x) - W29/2, with a_y/b_y taken from the fitted street line at that x. W8 = 213.09 px and W29 = 214.75 px are the widths of a printed 70-ft avenue MEASURED ON THE SAME SHEET (sheet 8: the 70-ft avenue bounding block 379 on the west, three measurements 213.46/213.97/211.84; sheet 29: Av. H East, three measurements 214.64/214.68/214.94). Both correspond to 70.4 and 70.7 ft at each sheet's own scale-bar ppf, confirming the printed 70' in Av. G on both sheets. Consequence: a_x and b_x are constructions, NOT drawn ink - do not expect to see a feature there. The raw drawn frontage points, if you prefer them, are (sheet 8 -> sheet 29): (3102.41,115.31)->(254.29,112.50), (3101.19,361.54)->(256.95,360.27), (3096.53,1284.79)->(267.71,1291.04), (3098.52,1529.31)->(270.44,1535.28), (3090.27,2448.29)->(277.69,2465.65), (3086.90,2694.15)->(281.98,2710.43), (3087.45,3617.81)->(288.15,3640.34), (3087.60,3864.84)->(289.78,3886.87); these are 70 ft apart in ground and must not be paired directly.

ERROR BUDGET. The avenue-width assumption is almost entirely SYSTEMATIC and is absorbed by tx: re-solving with W8/W29 = 211.82/212.67 (nominal 70 ft x each sheet's scale-bar ppf) or with 210.0/216.0 changes tx by less than 1.7 px and leaves scale, rotation and rms unchanged to 6 significant figures. If Av. G is really, say, 68 ft rather than 70 ft on both sheets, tx moves by ~6 px and nothing else moves. The per-point RANDOM error is dominated by the drafting wobble of the two frontage lines (sheet 8's frontage x wanders 3086.9-3102.4 down the sheet, sheet 29's 254.3-289.8 monotonically), which is why 3.5 px is stated for the six drawn corners rather than the ~0.7 px the fits alone would suggest. L0 and L7 have no drawn corner at the seam - the frontage line had to be extrapolated ~250 px beyond the last block - hence 5.5 px.

SELF-CHECK. The similarity maps sheet 8 -> sheet 29 as b = s*R(theta)*a + t with R = [[cos,-sin],[sin,cos]] in image coordinates (x right, y DOWN); theta = -0.8068 deg therefore means sheet 8's content must be turned 0.81 deg anticlockwise on screen to match sheet 29. Weighted by 1/uncertainty^2. Residuals per point (L0..L7): 1.63, 1.37, 1.54, 2.31, 3.35, 5.21, 2.46, 5.10 px. Largest residual/uncertainty ratio is 1.49, so no point is an outlier by the 3x rule. The fitted scale 1.00728 sits 0.33% above the ratio of the two measured scale bars (3.0382/3.026 = 1.00403); the sheets' own drawn content agrees with the fit rather than with the bars - sheet 29's blocks measure 802 px wide and 930 px deep against sheet 8's 790 x 923, a content ratio of 1.008-1.015.

THE IMPORTANT CAVEAT - THIS SEAM CANNOT SETTLE THE ROTATION. All eight correspondences are collinear (they lie on the Av. G centreline), which is unavoidable: there is no drawn overlap anywhere off that line. A similarity is still determined (nullity 0), but its rotation is fixed entirely by the ALONG-seam direction, i.e. by the N-S line family. The E-W family tells a different story. Mean bearing of the vertical (avenue) family: +0.226 deg on sheet 8, -0.539 deg on sheet 29 -> relative rotation -0.765 deg. Mean bearing of the horizontal (street) family, from the eight fitted street lines: -0.025 deg on sheet 8, -0.317 deg on sheet 29 -> relative rotation -0.292 deg. Each sheet's own drawn grid is thus non-orthogonal by about 0.25 deg (sheet 8 +0.251, sheet 29 -0.222), in opposite senses, and the two families disagree about the S8|S29 relative rotation by ~0.47 deg. My -0.807 deg is the N-S answer because that is the only direction my collinear control can see; a solve that also uses the shared E-W street lines as direction constraints will and should pull it toward -0.5 deg. I recommend adding the eight shared E-W street property lines of this seam to config/line_constraints.yaml as a direction family; they are the only evidence on this seam about the other axis. Do NOT read the 3.22 px rms as meaning the seam is solved to 3 px in all respects - it is 3 px ALONG and ACROSS the avenue centreline, and comparatively uninformative about rotation.
